cur:catacombs-louvre-teaching-ma2958.summary: Christ sits enthroned at the centre, raising his hand as he teaches, while the apostles sit on either side in two animated rows, scrolls in hand, turning towards him. The composition, taken from images of philosophers and their pupils, proclaims Christ as the one true Teacher.
facts: Commons records that it was found at Rignieux-le-Franc (Ain), in eastern France.
The Louvre's photographer describes the main face as 'Christ enthroned at the centre teaching the apostles'.

cur:catacombs-ravenna-rinaldo-sarcophagu.summary: Between palm trees, Christ is seated at the centre holding a book, while Peter and Paul bow towards him from either side, offering wreaths. The scaly, rounded lid is typical of Ravenna. Carved in the 5th century, the sarcophagus was later reused for the 14th-century archbishop Rinaldo da Concorreggio.
facts: Commons dates the sarcophagus to the 5th century; Rinaldo da Concorreggio was archbishop of Ravenna (died 1321).
It stands in the Chapel of the Madonna del Sudore in the cathedral.
cur:catacombs-ravenna-rinaldo-sarcophagu.notes: The apostles' identification as Peter and Paul is the usual reading.
